\[
\begin{gathered}
h[n] = \frac{2 f_c \operatorname{sinc}\!\big(2 f_c (n - M)\big)\, w[n]}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} 2 f_c \operatorname{sinc}\!\big(2 f_c (k - M)\big)\, w[k]},
\qquad
M = \frac{N-1}{2},
\\[4pt]
I_{\text{out}}(x,y) = \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} h[i]\, h[j]\, I(x+i-M,\, y+j-M),
\qquad
N = 15, \quad f_c = 0.15
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(h[n]\): Tap n of the 1D filter
- \(N\): Number of taps, odd
- \(M\): Index of the center tap
- \(f_c\): Cutoff frequency in cycles per pixel
- \(\operatorname{sinc}(t)\): sin(pi t) / (pi t), and 1 at t = 0
- \(w[n]\): The window value at tap n
- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output channel value

The ideal low-pass filter has the sinc function as its taps, but they never end. The window w tapers them to N taps. Dividing by the sum makes the gain at frequency 0 exactly 1, so flat areas keep their value. The 2D filter applies the same taps along rows and columns.
